references.text: Jeremiah prophesies that the bodies of the dead shall become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, with no one to drive them away—the same wording and judgment as in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah repeats the warning that corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth as part of God's judgment.
God warns through Jeremiah that enemies will give their dead bodies as food to the birds and the animals.
Those who break the covenant shall have their dead bodies given to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
Goliath threatens David with giving his flesh to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field, and David responds with the same threat—showing how this was a known curse.
The prophecy concerning the house of Jeroboam that those who die shall be eaten by birds and dogs—a similar judgment upon the wicked.
The same judgment is pronounced against the house of Baasha—the birds and the dogs shall eat the dead.
The judgment against the house of Ahab repeats that birds and dogs shall eat the dead.
Ezekiel prophesies concerning Gog that he will be given as food to birds of prey and wild animals.
The psalmist laments that the bodies of God's servants have been given to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth—the fulfillment of the curse.
John sees in his vision that the birds are called to eat the flesh of kings, commanders, and all people—an eschatological fulfillment of the curse.
